## Issues found in `taskq/`

1. **`taskq/queue.py:4`** — Mutable default argument `items=[]` causes shared state across `TaskQueue` instances.
2. **`taskq/queue.py:10`** — `is_full()` uses `>` instead of `>=`, so the queue accepts one task beyond `capacity`.
3. **`taskq/worker.py:11`** — Log file is opened but never closed; leaks a file descriptor.
4. **`taskq/worker.py:19-20`** — Exceptions are silently swallowed; failures are logged neither to the log nor anywhere else.
5. **`taskq/scheduler.py:10-18`** — `run_with_retry` ignores `should_retry`, and returns `None` after max retries without distinguishing success/failure or re-raising.
6. **`taskq/scheduler.py:20-21`** — `should_retry` accepts an `attempt` parameter but `run_with_retry` does not use or expose it consistently.
7. **`taskq/store.py:15-17`** — `find_by_name` uses string formatting into the SQL query, creating SQL injection vulnerability.
